question: Which of the following was a non-violent protest against the British monopoly on salt production in 1930?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandi March**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Dandi March**, also known as the Salt March, was a non-violent protest led by Mahatma Gandhi from March 12 to April 6, 1930, against the British monopoly on salt production.
 
• It was part of the broader **Civil Disobedience Movement** and aimed at breaking the British Salt Law by producing salt from seawater.
 
• The march started from **Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad** and ended at Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat, covering approximately 390 kilometers.
 
• Thousands of people joined Gandhi on this march, making it a significant event in India's struggle for independence.
 
• The Dandi March marked the beginning of widespread acts of defiance against British laws and inspired millions to join the freedom movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salt Law:**

 
 
• The British Salt Law imposed a monopoly on salt production and prohibited Indians from collecting or selling salt independently.
 
• Salt, a basic necessity, was heavily taxed, making it expensive for common people.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Gandhi in 1930, it involved non-violent resistance and refusal to obey unjust laws imposed by the British government.
 
• The Dandi March was the first major act of this movement, which later expanded to include boycotts of British goods and institutions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Dandi March:**
 
 
• It drew global attention to India's independence struggle and showcased the power of non-violent protest.
 
• The march unified people across social and economic barriers and strengthened the resolve for self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Key Participants:**
 
 
• Besides Gandhi, notable leaders like Sarojini Naidu and thousands of followers participated in the march.
 
• Women played a significant role in the movement, symbolizing their increasing involvement in the freedom struggle.
